subject: Request: temporary SLO tolerance and mitigation options for model-6z latency drift
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@finpay.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: james.oneill@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Request: temporary SLO tolerance for model-6z latency drift

Hi Rachel / Marcus,

Quick summary: starting ~11:30 UTC today we've observed a sustained jump in p95 latency for model-6z on our production traffic — baseline p95 has historically been ~170-220ms, and we're seeing values around 480-520ms for the last 90 minutes. Throughput and error rates look stable, but this latency shift is causing timeouts in a couple of our orchestration flows.

Attached is a short CSV with the p95 histogram and a Grafana link showing the spike. Can Redwood either:
- revert FinPay traffic to the model-6y variant (same weights) as an immediate mitigation, or
- approve a temporary SLO tolerance (p95 up to 600ms) while you investigate and stabilize model-6z.

We appreciate quick input — this is impacting a customer-facing batch job and we need a mitigation plan in the next 2 hours if possible.

Attachments: finpay_p95_report_20271207.csv

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez
Engineering Lead, FinPay
sofia@finpay.com
From: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@finpay.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James O'Neill <james.oneill@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 17:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO tolerance for model-6z latency drift

Sofia — thanks for the heads up and for the fast data. I've looped in Marcus and our on-call ops lead (cc'd above) and sketched an immediate mitigation plan:

1) Roll a targeted canary routing of FinPay production traffic to model-6y (compatible variant) — this should be reversible within minutes.
2) Apply a temporary SLO tolerance window of 72 hours (p95 up to 600ms) while we root cause.
3) If we detect an increasing error rate (>1% over 1h) or p95 > 800ms for the last 30m, we'll trigger an automatic rollback of all FinPay traffic to the last-known-good model and alert your team.

Before we enact the canary we need explicit OK from your side to proceed with the variant fallback and we need internal approval for the SLO carve-out (commercial sign-off). I've attached a short mitigation note.

Attachments: proposed-mitigation.md

Rachel Kim
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, Sofia Martinez <sofia@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2027 18:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO tolerance for model-6z latency drift

Rachel — thanks. FYI this is deal FP-8421 (FinPay scale rollout). Commercials: a 72-hour tolerance is acceptable from our side if we pair it with the rollback triggers and documentation that we can later use for crediting if needed.

Lauren — can you review and, if okay, confirm we can approve the 72-hour SLO carve-out and draft the short amendment (SLO carve-out + rollback conditions)? I'll notify the FinPay procurement/legal teams once we have sign-off.

Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 01:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO tolerance for model-6z latency drift

Marking this approved with conditions. Approve a 72-hour temporary SLO tolerance window for FinPay (p95 <= 600ms) with the following required controls:

- Automatic rollback trigger if error rate > 1% sustained over a 1 hour window, OR if p95 > 800ms for the last 30 minutes.
- Operations to run the canary fallback to model-6y at 25% traffic first, monitor for 30 minutes, then escalate to 100% if stable.
- Legal to append a one-paragraph SLO carve-out amendment to the existing FP-8421 contract; include language for pro-rated credits if we miss roll-back SLAs.
- DocuSign prepared for signatures; include the start/end timestamps for the tolerance window.

I've created a draft amendment and uploaded it to DocuSign. Link below.

Signature:
Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 02:33:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary SLO tolerance for model-6z latency drift

Forwarding full thread to ops — Lauren has approved a 72-hour tolerance (p95 <= 600ms) with rollback conditions. Action items for Ops (please confirm ETA):

- Start a 25% canary shift of FinPay production traffic to model-6y immediately; monitor p95 and error rate for 30m.
- If canary is stable, escalate to 100% and keep the SLO tolerance window open for 72 hours from the time of canary start.
- Implement automatic rollback if (a) error rate >1% over 1h OR (b) p95 > 800ms sustained for 30m.
- Attach monitoring dashboards to JIRA OPS-7123 and notify FinPay via this thread when the canary starts and when complete.

Ops: please attach runbook excerpts to the JIRA ticket and confirm when done.
